payload.acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] claim on a closed record exits non-zero, appends nothing and names the reopen command.
- [ ] claim on an open or deferred record still works.
payload.description:
## Trigger

When someone runs claim on a record that is already closed, I want the claim refused by name with the reopen command, so I can never move finished work back to in progress by mistake.

## Context

2026-09-25: python3 .basicly/core/kit/tracker/cli.py claim .basicly/ledger basicly-zem45s8 on the closed record appended an assignee event and a status in_progress event, with no refusal. The record read in_progress until it was closed again.
payload.requirements: A claim never changes the status of a closed record.
payload.title: claim reopens a closed record

payload.acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] The fix text asks the person to name which repositories are private, or suggests an entry that trusts the owner's repositories and asks before private content goes into a public one.
- [ ] A test pins the new wording.
payload.description:
## Trigger

When permissions-check reports a one-repo auto mode trust list, I want its fix to keep private and public repositories apart, so I can follow the fix without letting private content move into a public repository unchecked.

## Context

Review from the development session, 2026-09-25: the fix text suggests 'Source control: github.com/<owner> and all repos under it'. The owner holds private and public repositories, so an owner-wide entry trusts both alike.
payload.requirements: A suggested fix never widens trust across a private and public boundary in silence.
payload.title: the auto mode trust fix suggests trusting every repo of the owner

payload.acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] The loader refuses an allow rule for each program named in the context.
- [ ] A table-driven test holds the list.
payload.description:
## Trigger

When someone adds an allow rule to the catalog, I want the loader to refuse any rule whose program runs another program, so I can never ship a rule that auto mode drops or that grants arbitrary execution.

## Context

Review from the development session, 2026-09-25: INTERPRETERS, PACKAGE_MANAGERS and COMMAND_WRAPPERS in src/basicly/permissions.py miss timeout, nohup, nice, ionice, stdbuf, command, builtin, time, doas, su, runuser, make, just, awk and gawk, and the exec forms of find and sed.
payload.requirements: One list of programs that run another program, used by the loader.
payload.title: the auto mode drop check misses programs that run another program

payload.acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] permissions-check notes when basicly is not on the PATH and names uv tool install as the fix.
- [ ] The permissions how-to states the condition.
payload.description:
## Trigger

When a repository runs basicly as uv run basicly or through uvx, I want permissions-check to say that the shipped basicly allow rules match nothing, so I can install basicly on the path or know why I am still asked.

## Context

Review from the development session, 2026-09-25: 16 of the 22 narrow rules name basicly, and auto mode drops uv and uvx forms, so the rules match only when basicly is on the PATH.
payload.requirements: The note is advisory and changes no exit code.
payload.title: say that the basicly allow rules need basicly on the path
